title: Polite address, requests and greetings
goal: Switch between familiar and polite registers and use the stock greetings and wishes.

blocks.text: Politeness in Greek is carried by grammar more than by vocabulary: the **polite plural** (εσείς to one person), the **conditional θα ήθελα**, **να**-requests, the softening **λίγο**, and **μπορώ** questions. The exam's speaking paper rewards switching registers cleanly, so practise both.

blocks.title: Η καινούργια γειτόνισσα
blocks.setting: Myrto has just moved into a block of flats in Patras; on the stairs she meets her elderly neighbour, Mr Antonis.

lines.el: Καλησπέρα σας! Με συγχωρείτε, εσείς μένετε στον δεύτερο;
lines.en: Good evening! Excuse me, do you live on the second floor?

lines.el: Καλησπέρα. Ναι, εγώ είμαι, ο Αντώνης. Εσείς πρέπει να είστε η καινούργια κοπέλα από τον τρίτο.
lines.en: Good evening. Yes, that's me, Antonis. You must be the new young lady from the third floor.

lines.el: Ναι, η Μυρτώ. Χαίρω πολύ. Μετακόμισα την Κυριακή.
lines.en: Yes, I'm Myrto. Pleased to meet you. I moved in on Sunday.

lines.el: Καλώς ορίσατε στην πολυκατοικία μας! Αν χρειαστείτε κάτι, μη διστάσετε να χτυπήσετε την πόρτα μου.
lines.en: Welcome to our building! If you need anything, don't hesitate to knock on my door.

lines.el: Ευχαριστώ πολύ, είστε πολύ ευγενικός. Μάλιστα, θα ήθελα να σας ζητήσω μια χάρη, αν δεν σας πειράζει.
lines.en: Thank you so much, that's very kind of you. In fact, I'd like to ask you a favour, if you don't mind.

lines.el: Αύριο περιμένω ένα δέμα, αλλά θα λείπω στη δουλειά. Μήπως θα μπορούσατε να το παραλάβετε εσείς;
lines.en: Tomorrow I'm expecting a parcel, but I'll be out at work. Could you possibly take it in for me?

lines.el: Ευχαρίστως. Είμαι συνταξιούχος, όλη μέρα σπίτι είμαι. Μόνο μια παράκληση...
lines.en: Gladly. I'm retired, I'm at home all day. Just one request...

lines.el: Μη μου μιλάς στον πληθυντικό, κορίτσι μου, με κάνεις να νιώθω εκατό χρονών! Να μιλάμε στον ενικό;
lines.en: Don't talk to me in the plural, my girl, you make me feel a hundred! Shall we say εσύ?
All right, Mr Antonis, as you like!

lines.el: Έτσι μπράβο. Και τι είναι το δέμα, αν επιτρέπεται;
lines.en: That's more like it. And what's in the parcel, if I may ask?

lines.el: Βιβλία, για τη δουλειά μου. Είναι βαρύ, οπότε πες στον κούριερ να το αφήσει στην πόρτα σου και θα το πάρω εγώ το βράδυ.
lines.en: Books, for my work. It's heavy, so tell the courier to leave it at your door and I'll pick it up in the evening.

lines.el: Σύμφωνοι. Και όταν έρθεις, πέρασε να πιεις κι ένα κρασάκι. Η γυναίκα μου, η κυρία Λίτσα, θα χαρεί να σε γνωρίσει.
lines.en: Agreed. And when you come, stop by for a glass of wine. My wife, Mrs Litsa, will be glad to meet you.

lines.el: Με μεγάλη χαρά! Να φέρω κάτι;
lines.en: With great pleasure! Shall I bring anything?

lines.el: Τίποτα, μόνο τον εαυτό σου. Καλό βράδυ, Μυρτώ, και καλορίζικο το καινούργιο σπίτι!
lines.en: Nothing, just yourself. Good evening, Myrto, and may the new home bring you luck!

lines.el: Ευχαριστώ για όλα! Καληνύχτα, κύριε Αντώνη, τα λέμε αύριο!
lines.en: Thanks for everything! Good night, Mr Antonis, see you tomorrow!

gloss.Χαίρω: χαίρω — Χαίρω πολύ = pleased to meet you
gloss.επιτρέπεται: επιτρέπεται — it is allowed; αν επιτρέπεται = if I may ask
gloss.εαυτό: εαυτός — self; μόνο τον εαυτό σου = just yourself
gloss.καλορίζικο: καλορίζικος — wish for a new home or purchase: may it bring luck

Τι ζητάει ο κύριος Αντώνης από τη Μυρτώ;
Ποια φράση της Μυρτώς είναι η πιο ευγενική;

questions.prompt: Ο κύριος Αντώνης λέει «Πείτε μου». Σε ποιο πρόσωπο μιλάει;

blocks.title: Να μιλάμε στον ενικό;
blocks.text: In Greece **εσείς** is the default with strangers, officials, doctors and anyone clearly older, while shop staff and customers of similar age often move quickly to **εσύ**. The switch is usually offered by the older or more senior person: **Να μιλάμε στον ενικό;** 'shall we use the singular?'. Address can be asymmetric: an elderly neighbour says **εσύ** to a young woman she has known since childhood, often adding **κορίτσι μου** or **παιδί μου**, while she answers with **εσείς**. Respect can also come with first names: **κυρία Μαρία**, **κύριε Γιώργο** is polite and warm at the same time.

blocks.title: Στο φαρμακείο
blocks.en:
— Good morning.
— Good morning. What would you like?
— I'd like something for my throat. It's been sore since last night.
— Do you have a temperature as well?
— No, I don't think so. Just a bit of a cough.
— Could you tell me if you're taking any other medicine?
— I only take vitamins.
— All right. I suggest these lozenges. Take one every three hours, but no more than six a day. And drink lots of hot drinks, tea with honey for example.
— Can I take them before bed as well?
— Yes, that's no problem.

— Thank you very much. Could you possibly give me a bag as well?
— Of course. Would you like anything else?
— No, that's all. How much are they?
— Eight euros fifty.
— Here you are. Sorry, I've only got a twenty.
— That's fine, I have change. Here's your change. If it doesn't get better in three days, you should go to a doctor, all right?
— All right. Thanks for everything.
— Not at all. Get well soon!

At the door Eleni meets her neighbour, Mrs Ritsa.
— Good morning, Mrs Ritsa! How are you?
— Eleni dear! I'm well, my child. And you? What's wrong?
— Nothing serious, my throat.
— Come round this afternoon and I'll make you a tea with honey!

gloss.ενικό: ενικός — singular (acc.); στον ενικό = using εσύ
gloss.πληθυντικό: πληθυντικός — plural (acc.); στον πληθυντικό = using εσείς
gloss.Τίποτα: τίποτα — not at all (reply to thanks)
gloss.έπαθες: παθαίνω — happened to you (Τι έπαθες; = What's wrong?)
gloss.θέλατε: θέλω — (would) like: Τι θα θέλατε; = What would you like?

items.prompt: Wait a moment, please. (soft request)
Make it polite: *Τι θέλεις;*
items.why: Polite plural: 2pl verb; θα θέλατε is softer still.

items.prompt: Make it polite: *Κάθισε!*
items.why: Polite plural imperative of κάθομαι: καθίστε.

items.prompt: Make it polite: *Πού μένεις;*
items.why: 2pl present for one person addressed politely.

items.prompt: Make it polite: *Μπορείς να μου πεις την ώρα;*
items.answer: Μπορείτε να μου πείτε την ώρα;
accept: Μπορείτε να μου πείτε την ώρα
Θα μπορούσατε να μου πείτε την ώρα
items.why: Both verbs go into the plural: μπορείτε, πείτε.

items.prompt: Make it polite: *Περίμενε λίγο!*
items.why: Plural imperative περιμένετε; λίγο softens the request.

items.prompt: Make it polite: *Πάρε με τηλέφωνο.*
items.why: Plural perfective imperative of παίρνω: πάρτε.

items.prompt: Say politely in Greek: *I would like the bill.*
items.why: θα ήθελα is the polite 'I'd like'; λογαριασμός in the accusative.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *Shall we use εσύ?* (lit. speak in the singular)
items.why: να + continuous for a new, ongoing arrangement.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *Excuse me...* (to a stranger, to get attention)
items.why: Polite plural συγχωρείτε; συγγνώμη also works.

items.prompt: Polite wish to someone who is ill:
items.why: σας makes the wish polite or plural.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *Welcome!* (polite, or to several people)
items.why: Plural forms for polite address; to a friend: καλώς ήρθες / καλώς όρισες.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *Have a good day!* (polite)
items.why: σας turns the wish polite; the reply is Επίσης!

items.prompt: To your doctor: 'Do you have time tomorrow?'
items.why: A doctor gets the polite plural (2pl).

items.prompt: To one woman, politely: 'Are you tired?'
items.why: In the polite plural the verb is plural but an adjective agrees with the real person: singular.

items.prompt: The softest request:
items.answer: Θα μπορούσατε να κλείσετε το παράθυρο;
options: Θα μπορούσατε να κλείσετε το παράθυρο;
items.why: θα + past (θα μπορούσατε) is the most tentative way to ask.

items.prompt: Reply to 'Ευχαριστώ πολύ!'
items.why: παρακαλώ = 'you're welcome'; ορίστε is for handing something over.

items.prompt: Handing something over: 'Here you are.'
items.why: ορίστε accompanies giving something (and also answers 'yes?' when called).

items.prompt: Reply to 'Καλή σας μέρα!' meaning 'You too!'
items.why: επίσης returns a wish.

items.prompt: An elderly neighbour to a young woman she has known for years:
items.why: Address can be asymmetric: the older person uses εσύ, the younger answers with εσείς.

items.prompt: Addressing Mr Papadopoulos directly:
items.why: Vocative: both κύριος and the -ος surname take -ε (Παπαδόπουλε).

items.prompt: Mr Antonis to Myrto: *Don't talk to me in the plural!*
items.why: μη + imperfective for a general 'stop doing that'; μη is fine before μ, though μην also occurs.

items.prompt: Switch to εσύ, as Myrto does: *Πείτε στον κούριερ να το αφήσει στην πόρτα σας.*
